newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seguin may seek French presidency.
newsitem.headline: Seguin may seek French presidency.

text.p: An ally of Philippe Seguin, rising star of the RPR Gaullist party, hinted strongly on Saturday that Seguin might stand in France's next presidential election in which President Jacques Chirac is widely thought to want to seek re-election.
"It is useful that several eminent people in the RPR (Rally for the Republic) aim for the highest job in the land," said former Gaullist Interior Minister and Seguin ally Charles Pasqua.
"We will see what the needs are when we get there (at election time). If Jacques Chirac wants to stand again, then of course, we should back him," Pasqua told Europe One radio.
Philippe Seguin became RPR parliamentary floor leader this month, a key step in his bid to seize the party presidency from ex-premier Alain Juppe after the party's June 1 election defeat.

Seguin emerged in the final days of the snap election campaign as Chirac's favourite to succeed the unpopular Juppe as prime minister but Chirac and Seguin are nonetheless thought to be on poor terms.
Chirac, who created the RPR two decades ago as a vehicle to bring him to power, still has five years of his seven-year-term to run.
He sought to block Seguin's bid to take over the party, possibly for fear Seguin might seek to use it in the same way as he did.
Pasqua said he expected the party would change its name soon.
